text:
Jason Dickinson scored against his old team on Saturday, a revenge-game goal against Vancouver in a 4-2 Oilers win that Oilersnation's instant reaction led with. It was the latest small moment for a veteran who has played for Dallas, Vancouver and Chicago before landing in Edmonton.

Four points in nine games is more than anyone expected from him, and it won't last at this rate: he has two goals on eight shots, a 25% shooting percentage. The bigger concern is five on five, where Edmonton has taken just 37% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 13 points worse than without him. His minutes have dropped by nearly three a night lately.

That isn't the whole story of his game. Evolving-Hockey had his value last season coming from defense, with opponents getting fewer chances against him than against 86% of forwards, while he faced the toughest competition in the league (98th percentile) with weak teammates in Chicago. That's a checking center's résumé. Our range has him at 6 to 15 goals over a full season. Edmonton needs him to get back to stopping goals, not scoring them.
headline: Dickinson's revenge goal
